overview: Rise 6.1.30's LongJump is a ModeValue shell registering ten movement modes (Vanilla, NCP, Vulcan, Extreme Craft, Fire Ball, Watchdog, Watchdog Fire Ball, Matrix (Deprecated), Sparky, Vulcan 2) with two shared shell-level toggles: Auto Disable (default on) turns the module off the tick the player lands after an air phase, and Fake Damage plays the local hurt animation. The mode families divide by mechanism: per-tick speed boosters that rewrite motion through the StrafeEvent stream (Vanilla, NCP, Sparky, Matrix), scripted launch sequences that emit explicit C03/C04 packets with timer scaling and S08 teleport cancels (Vulcan, Extreme Craft, Vulcan 2), and knockback-consumer launches that cancel the S12 self-velocity and convert it into forward motion (Watchdog, Fire Ball, Watchdog Fire Ball).

sections.p: The shell tracks an inAir flag from PreMotion and, when Auto Disable is on and the player touches ground after an air phase, toggles the module off on the spot; the Watchdog mode is exempt because its launch depends on the disable timing. onEnable runs PlayerUtil.fakeDamage when the Fake Damage toggle is set, which calls mc.thePlayer.handleHealthUpdate((byte) 2) and bumps the local health update counter: purely client-side hurt animation, zero packets. onDisable restores mc.timer.timerSpeed to 1.0. No packet is sent by the shell itself; every wire effect comes from the active mode.

VanillaLongJump, the default, is the minimal booster. Its StrafeEvent listener sets mc.thePlayer.motionY to the Height value (0.1 to 1, default 0.5) whenever the player is on the ground and calls event.setSpeed with the Speed value (0.1 to 9.5, default 1.0) on every strafe tick. setSpeed replaces the per-tick friction with the configured value (diagonal input applies 0.98 of it) and zeroes residual motion, so every movement tick runs at that magnitude. The boost rides the ordinary C03 movement stream with no extra packets. onDisable calls MoveUtil.stop() to kill residual motion.

NCPLongJump runs a bunny-friction stage machine keyed on offGroundTicks: tick 0 sets motionY to jumpMotion and speed to Ground Speed (default 0.4), tick 1 switches to Jump Speed (default 1.4), later ticks decay speed by MoveUtil.BUNNY_FRICTION (159), with a Timer setting (up to 10) and a glide adder of glide/100 per tick while falling. VulcanLongJump executes a fixed 6-tick script: tick 1 scales the timer to 0.5, emits three C04PacketPlayerPosition packets (pos, pos minus 0.0784000015258789, pos with onGround false), strafes at 7.9 and sets motionY 0.42; ticks 2 through 6 step motionY and the strafe down to 0.3, with an onGround spoof at tick 4, and every S08 teleport received while the script runs is cancelled. ExtremeCraftLongJump mirrors the C04 trio (pos, y minus 0.1, pos with onGround false) with timer 0.2 and strafe 3. SparkyLongJump scales the timer to 0.2, pushes setSpeed 9.2, emits C03PacketPlayer(true) packets and returns the timer to 0.5. WatchdogLongJump cancels the S12 self-velocity and converts its motionY into a manual lift, arms PacketlessDamageComponent, spoofs onGround (false always, true at offGroundTicks 1), scales the timer to 0.2 and parks keepalives through PingSpoofComponent.spoof(99999, ...) during the first five air ticks. FireBallLongJump and WatchdogFireballLongJump emit C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement for the held fireball item to trigger the launch, then consume the resulting S12 self-velocity into a 1.5 strafe.

files.label: LongJump.java (mode selector)
files.explanation: The ModeValue shell. It registers the ten mode classes, holds the Auto Disable and Fake Damage toggles, and runs the PreMotion listener that flips the inAir flag and toggles the module off on landing when Auto Disable is set. onEnable plays the local hurt animation through PlayerUtil.fakeDamage (handleHealthUpdate, no packet) when the toggle is on, and onDisable resets the timer speed. All packet activity lives in the mode classes under movement/longjump/.

files.label: VanillaLongJump.java (default mode)
files.explanation: The default mode and the simplest wire fingerprint: a StrafeEvent listener that lifts motionY to the Height value (default 0.5) on ground contact and asserts the Speed value (default 1.0, up to 9.5) on every strafe tick through event.setSpeed, which replaces the per-tick friction and zeroes residual motion so the next move runs at that magnitude. The boost is applied through the normal movement pipeline, so it travels inside the ordinary C03 stream as higher per-tick deltas rather than as extra packets. onDisable calls MoveUtil.stop(). The sibling NCP mode shows the more elaborate family: an offGroundTicks stage machine, timer scaling up to 10, and a glide adder of glide/100 per falling tick.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly rebuilds the client's physics envelope from the world rather than trusting the packets. The horizontal allowance comes from prepareSpeedEstimation and the vertical from vDistRel (line 1839), and the violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) plus max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) times 100 (line 233) with a set-back to the stored location. The longjump modes exceed both bounds at once: the scripted motionY tables (Vulcan's 0.42 then 0.1 lifts, ExtremeCraft's y-minus-0.1 claims) present vertical deltas outside vDistRel's four named envelopes (zero-y ground move, jump, step, riptide), and the horizontal strafes (Vulcan 7.9, Sparky 9.2, ExtremeCraft 3) run multiples of the survival horizontal allowance, which the speed-estimation path caps near MoveUtil.getAllowedHorizontalDistance. Ground-state spoofs do not help: fromOnGround and toOnGround come from RichBoundsLocation.isOnGround(), a block-cache scan at minY minus yOnGround, so a spoofed onGround flag never relaxes the envelope. The Watchdog mode's cancel-and-convert S12 handling is the one family this check does not directly flag, because the motion stays inside a legitimate knockback-shaped trajectory.

countering.label: Speed (horizontal accumulator)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's Speed check scores each move against the expected walking model: baseMove 0.2873 times the speed-potion multiplier, plus stage-based off-ground allowances and any pending velocity, with an instant cancel when a single move exceeds 8 blocks. The longjump boosters blow past the expected values: Vanilla's setSpeed 1.0 re-asserts full speed every tick on ground, NCP's Jump Speed 1.4 exceeds the ground expectation, Sparky's 9.2 setSpeed is above the 8-block instant-cancel line on a single tick, and Vulcan's 7.9 strafe sits just under it while still tripping the accumulated discrepancy. The check's on-ground accumulator also never resets between air ticks, so the sustained multi-tick boost accumulates violation instead of decaying.

countering.label: Speed (prev-speed progression)
countering.explanation: Hawk Speed predicts the next horizontal speed from the previous one: expected equals friction times lastSpeed times multipliers plus maxForce plus an epsilon, and only moves faster than expected accumulate discrepancy toward the 0.1 threshold. The longjump modes violate that progression by construction: the per-tick speed writes (event.setSpeed, MoveUtil.strafe) re-assert a constant magnitude every tick, so the prev-speed decay the model expects (friction near 0.91 per tick) never happens, and the stage machines that step speed upward mid-air (NCP tick 0 to tick 1, Vulcan's scripted sequence) present gains the model cannot derive from friction plus input force. The timer-scaled modes double the effect: at timer 2 the client covers two ticks of distance in one server tick, so the measured speed is roughly double the expected progression and the discrepancy accumulates each move.

countering.label: GroundSpoof (claimed vs predicted ground)
countering.explanation: Grim's GroundSpoof compares the claimed onGround flag against the post-prediction ground state: when the client reports a different value than the physics prediction derived from the last known ground, the check flags with a setback, with exemptions for spectator mode, exemptOnGround, block offsets and the tick after a teleport. It only bites the longjump modes that manipulate the flag: WatchdogLongJump sends onGround false on every tick and true at offGroundTicks 1, and VulcanLongJump claims onGround true at script tick 4 while mid-air; both present a claimed value that contradicts the predicted ground. The plain Vanilla mode and the pure motion boosters never touch the flag, so their onGround claims match the prediction and this check stays silent: an honest boundary for those modes.
